sections.h2: Where is the McDowell County registrar's office, and when is it open?
sections.html:
Go to 35 West Fort Street, or phone 828-652-4727. Weekday hours run 8:30am to 5:00pm, and McDowellDeeds.com carries the online services.

The county describes the office's work as recording, indexing and storing real estate and business documents. Marriage licenses, notary oaths, veterans' discharge records and certified birth and death copies come through the same door. Sellers care about the land side, where the registrar's stated aim is a public record that is complete, accurate and safe.

sections.h2: Can a McDowell County deed be filed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, and the county says all documents qualify. Three vendors are listed, so an attorney in another city can file without a trip to Marion.

Vendors named by McDowell County for electronic filing
VendorTelephone
Simplifile1-800-460-5657
Electronic Document Logistics (EDL)1-919-341-4101
Corporation Service Company (CSC)1-866-652-0111

The vendor choice belongs to your attorney or title company, which leaves you the job of having the signed deed ready.

sections.h2: What fees apply to a McDowell County deed filing?
sections.html:
The schedule in G.S. 161-10 governs here, with nothing added locally. The usual line items follow.

  • An ordinary deed: $26.00 through page 15, plus $4.00 a page after that.
  • A mortgage or deed of trust: $64.00 through page 35, plus $4.00 a page after that.
  • A lender's release: no charge.
  • A plat: $21.00 per sheet.
  • A certified copy: $5.00 for page one, $2.00 each after.
  • A nonstandard format: $25.00 extra. A second instrument inside one document: $10.00 extra.

Payment comes before filing. For a 60-page bundle of exhibits, phone 828-652-4727 and have the office total the charge.

sections.h2: Which side of a McDowell County sale pays the stamp tax?
sections.html:
Sellers carry this one. G.S. 105-228.30 sets $1.00 for every $500 of price, with any remainder under $500 counted as a full unit, and the registrar takes payment first.

The county general fund keeps one half. The rest moves to the state each month once refunds and the county's allowance are taken out.

Your closing statement prints the amount in the seller column, beside the loan payoff and any tax owed.

sections.h2: What happens to the parcel map once a McDowell County deed is filed?
sections.html:
On the assessor's page, GIS mapping is the unit that processes deed transfers and updates the maps, and it doubles as plat review officer. That puts deed transfers and parcel maps in the same hands, so check the map after your deed is recorded.

The assessor sits at 60 E. Court Street, open the same weekday hours, with separate extensions for real property, mapping and land records. A 2027 real property reappraisal is announced on that page, and new values will land on whoever owns the house then.

  • Ask mapping whether your parcel shows the shape and acreage you expect.
  • Ask real property staff what the reappraisal could do to your assessment.
  • Storm damage can be reported through a link on the assessor's page.

For a payoff on the current bill, call the tax collector at (828) 652-0701.

Tax Collections shares the County Services Building with the assessor, keeps the same 8:30am to 5:00pm weekday hours, and takes email at taxcollections@mcdowellnc.gov. It describes its job as collecting and accounting for county real and personal property tax. Two stops in one building, assessing and collecting, make it easy to settle the value question and the payoff question on the same trip.

sections.h2: Which relief programs on a McDowell County parcel affect a buyer?
sections.html:
Look for a relief program on the parcel early, since several of them end or come due at transfer. McDowell County's assessing office takes applications from January 1 through May 31 at 60 East Court Street, with everything due back by June 1, and an applicant may use only one program.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: takes off the larger of $25,000 or half the assessed value of the home and up to one acre, without a lien. The owner must be 65 by January 1 or totally disabled, and the county asks you to phone for the yearly income cap.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes $45,000 of assessed value on a one-time application, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: needs five preceding years of ownership and occupancy and an application each June 1. Three years of deferred tax sit as a lien, and a death, a transfer or leaving the home makes them payable.
  • Present-use value: for agricultural, forest or horticultural land, applied for in January, with a sound management plan for forest.

A parcel in present-use value or carrying deferred circuit breaker tax should be flagged to your closing attorney, so the back amounts are counted in the settlement.

sections.h2: How do McDowell County tax foreclosure auctions work?
sections.html:
Court-ordered tax foreclosures run under G.S. 105-374, and the auctions take place at the courthouse, 21 S. Main St. in Marion. The top bidder hands the commissioner $1,000.00 in cash when bidding closes.

Ten days follow for upset bids, filed with the clerk. Each must beat the previous bid by 5 percent and no less than $750.00, and each restarts the ten days. The county lists the clerk at (828) 655-4100.

  • Pending sales are listed on a link from the county's foreclosure page.
  • Map, assessed value, acreage and deed reference come from the GIS, searched by parcel number.
  • Wells and septic questions are left to the bidder to research, perhaps through a neighbor.

An owner behind on tax who sells first sidesteps the auction. Get the payoff figure from the tax collector while no sale date exists.

sections.h2: Why does filing order matter on a McDowell County house?
sections.html:
First to register wins priority. G.S. 47-18 withholds a deed's force against lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is filed where the land is located, which for a McDowell parcel means the Marion counter.

So attorneys send the deed and the buyer's loan papers together, and chase old releases too, since a lender's response time is the only cost of a cancellation. If a title search shows a lien nobody ever cancelled, have the attorney request the release early.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about McDowell County homeowners?
sections.html:
Census figures show 45,198 residents in mid-2025 versus 44,578 counted in 2020. There were 22,036 housing units in 2025 and 18,638 households across 2020 to 2024, 75.6 percent of homes being owner-occupied.

The median owner-occupied home was worth $171,100, gross rent was $806 at the median, and household income was $57,168 in 2024 dollars. Owners with a mortgage paid a median $1,161 a month in selected costs, against $328 for those without one. Builders drew 164 permits in 2025. The county has 2,760 veterans, some of whom may qualify for the exclusion in G.S. 105-277.1C.

Land covers 439.95 square miles, close to 101 people per square mile. Inherited houses, probate sales and homes needing work are common reasons to look at cash offers, and a cash buyer can close as soon as the deed is ready to file.

faqs.q: What days is the McDowell County registrar open?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, at 35 West Fort Street. The number is 828-652-4727.

faqs.q: Which vendors file McDowell County deeds electronically?
faqs.a: Simplifile, EDL (Electronic Document Logistics) and CSC (Corporation Service Company). The county says any document can go this way.

faqs.q: How much to file a 12-page deed in McDowell County?
faqs.a: $26.00, because the base fee reaches 15 pages. Deeds of trust have a $64.00 base through page 35.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the deed tax in McDowell County?
faqs.a: The seller, at $1.00 per $500 of price, paid at the counter ahead of filing.

faqs.q: What is the minimum upset bid at a McDowell County tax sale?
faqs.a: Five percent over the last bid, with a floor of $750.00 more. The clerk's office takes it, and the ten-day clock starts over.
